batch.untrusted: The SSH host fingerprint is not verified. Verify it on the host details page before adding this host to a batch
hint.commands: Commands run on the remote host:
hint.test_effect: Effect: signs in with the saved password or key and only reads system information (uname, /etc/os-release) to detect the package manager. Nothing on the host changes.
hint.test_risk: Risk: low. After fingerprint verification, your SSH credentials are sent to this host; make sure the address is correct.
hint.probe_effect: Effect: performs only the SSH handshake to read the server key fingerprint. No user name, password or key is sent and no command runs.
hint.probe_risk: Risk: trusting a wrong fingerprint sends later credentials to an impostor. Verify the fingerprint through another channel.
hint.check_effect: Effect: refreshes package indexes as root (through sudo for other accounts), then lists available updates. Nothing is installed or removed.
hint.check_risk: Risk: the sudo password is sent over the SSH channel's standard input. Writes the package index cache as root and briefly holds the package manager lock, so other package operations may wait. Times out after 5 minutes.
hint.upgrade_effect: Effect: refreshes package indexes, then upgrades every upgradable package non-interactively as root (through sudo for other accounts). APT keeps existing config files, only lists services needing restart and never installs new dependencies or removes packages; DNF/YUM may install or remove packages to satisfy dependencies and save new config files as .rpmnew; pkg upgrades dependencies too.
hint.upgrade_risk: Risk: changes the remote system and cannot be undone automatically. Services may restart or be interrupted, new kernels need a reboot, and new versions may be incompatible. A dropped connection or the 30-minute timeout can leave the package database half-configured. Closing this app does not stop an upgrade already running on the host.
hint.batch_check_effect: Effect: refreshes package indexes and reads pending updates on every selected host at once (up to 8 in parallel) and saves each result separately. Root accounts do not use sudo.
hint.batch_check_risk: Risk: each host's sudo password is sent over its own SSH standard input. Indexes are refreshed as root while holding the package manager lock. One host failing does not affect the others.
hint.batch_upgrade_title: Batch {manager} upgrade (uses sudo, changes several systems)
hint.batch_upgrade_effect: Effect: refreshes indexes and upgrades available packages non-interactively on every selected host at once (up to 8 in parallel). Root accounts do not use sudo. Every host uses the same package manager and commands.
hint.batch_upgrade_risk: Risk: changes several systems at once and cannot be undone automatically; services may restart or be interrupted on all of them together. Upgrade a single test host first, and avoid upgrading every node of one cluster at the same time.
hint.delete_effect: Effect: removes this host's connection data, credentials, fingerprint and results from the local host store only. Nothing connects to or changes the remote host.
hint.delete_risk: Risk: deletion cannot be undone; saved passwords and keys must be entered again.
upgrade.title: Confirm {manager} upgrade · {count} host(s)
upgrade.batch_notice: A batch upgrade connects to every selected host at once. Each host's result is saved separately and shown on the batch page.
upgrade.ack: I understand this changes the remote systems as root and cannot be undone automatically

batch.undetected: Package manager not detected yet; use “Test connection” or check updates on the host page first

hint.detect_note: Package manager not detected yet: the system is detected first, then the APT, DNF, YUM or FreeBSD pkg index refresh and listing run accordingly (through sudo for other accounts).
